statement: The four-digit number 6_72 is divisible by both 4 and 9. Which digit goes in the gap?

choices.misconception: I used the test for 3 instead of the test for 9 and picked the smallest digit that passed.
I left the 7 out when adding the digits, so I made 6 + 2 + 1 = 9.
I thought a number divisible by 4 must have the digit 4 in it.
I left the 6 out when adding the digits, so I made 7 + 2 + 9 = 18.

hints: Each divisibility test looks at a different part of the number.
The test for 4 looks only at the last two digits; the test for 9 looks at the sum of all the digits. Check the test for 4, then make the digit sum a multiple of 9.
72 is a multiple of 4 whatever the missing digit is. The other digits add to 6 + 7 + 2 = 15, and the next multiple of 9 is 18.

solutions.reliable: Divisible by 4: the last two digits, 72, make a multiple of 4 (72 = 4 x 18), so every digit in the gap passes. Divisible by 9: the digit sum must be a multiple of 9. 6 + 7 + 2 = 15, so 15 plus the missing digit must be 18 (reaching 27 would need 12, which is not a digit). So the digit is 3, and indeed 6372 = 9 x 708 = 4 x 1593. The transferable idea: when a number must pass two tests, apply each test to the part of the number it looks at.

whyOnTest: Missing-digit questions test the divisibility rules directly, and the rule for 3 is the tempting wrong tool.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
